title: Lesson 1: Creating lists
lessonSummary: Great! You created lists and measured their length.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: An empty list, a text list and a number list.
tasks.codeTemplate:
leer = []
horses = ["Stormwind", "Lightning", "Luna", "Fox", "Balu"]
zahlen = [1, 5, 10, 15, 20]
print(f"Empty: {leer}")
print(f"List: {horses}")
print(f"Numbers: {zahlen}")
print(f"Count: {len(horses)}")

tasks.instruction: Create a list horses with the five texts Stormwind, Lightning, Luna, Fox and Balu (in this order). Then print exactly Count: 5 by using len().
Create an empty list called empty. Then print Empty: [] (put the list into the text) and on the next line Length: 0 (with len()).

title: Lesson 2: Accessing entries
lessonSummary: Nice! You access entries by index and can change them.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: First and last entry and a list inside a list.
tasks.codeTemplate:
horses = ["Stormwind", "Lightning", "Luna", "Fox", "Balu"]
print(f"First: {horses[0]}")
print(f"Last: {horses[-1]}")
party = [["Anna", "Jumping", 15], ["Ben", "Dressage", 12]]
print(f"Name of the second: {party[1][0]}")

tasks.instruction: The list horses is provided. Print the second entry as Second: Lightning and the second to last as Second to last: Fox (using the indices 1 and -2).

validation.expected:
Second: Lightning
Second to last: Fox

tasks.instruction: The list horses is provided. Replace the first entry with Stella and print the list with print(). It must then look like this: ['Stella', 'Lightning', 'Luna', 'Fox', 'Balu']
The list horses is provided. Print the first three entries with a slice [0:3] and on the next line the last two with [-2:]: ['Stormwind', 'Lightning', 'Luna'] and ['Fox', 'Balu']

title: Lesson 3: Adding entries
lessonSummary: Great! Your lists grow with append() and insert().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: append, insert and joining two lists with +.
tasks.codeTemplate:
horses = ["Stormwind", "Lightning", "Luna"]
horses.append("Nova")
horses.insert(0, "Stella")
print(horses)
mehr = horses + ["Rex"]
print(f"Joined: {mehr}")

tasks.instruction: The list horses is provided. Use append() to add Nova and then Rex and print the list. It must look like this: ['Stormwind', 'Lightning', 'Luna', 'Nova', 'Rex']
The list horses is provided. Use insert() to put the entry Stella at the start (index 0) and print exactly First: Stella (using horses[0]).
The list horses is provided. Attach the three entries Nova, Rex and Mila in one go with extend() and print exactly Count: 6 (len).

title: Lesson 4: Removing entries
lessonSummary: Nice! You can remove entries on purpose.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: remove, pop and pop(0).
tasks.codeTemplate:
horses = ["Stormwind", "Lightning", "Luna", "Fox", "Balu"]
horses.remove("Fox")
letzter = horses.pop()
erster = horses.pop(0)
print(f"Removed: {letzter} and {erster}")
print(horses)

tasks.instruction: The list horses is provided. Use remove() to remove the entry Fox and print the list. It must look like this: ['Stormwind', 'Lightning', 'Luna', 'Balu']
The list horses is provided. Take the last element out with pop() and store it in removed. Print exactly Removed: Balu and on the next line Left: 4 (len).

title: Lesson 5: Searching and counting
lessonSummary: Great! You find entries, check whether they exist and count them.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: in, index and count.
tasks.codeTemplate:
horses = ["Stormwind", "Lightning", "Stormwind", "Luna", "Stormwind", "Fox"]
print(f"Contained: {"Lightning" in horses}")
print(f"Position: {horses.index("Lightning")}")
print(f"Count: {horses.count("Stormwind")}")

tasks.instruction: The list horses is provided. Check with in and print exactly Present: True for Lightning and on the next line Present: False for Nova.
The list horses (with duplicate entries) is provided. Print exactly Count Stormwind: 3 with count() and on the next line exactly Position Lightning: 1 with index().
The list horses (with duplicate entries) is provided. Create the list without duplicates with sorted(set(horses)) and print it: ['Fox', 'Lightning', 'Luna', 'Stormwind']

title: Lesson 6: Sorting
lessonSummary: Sorted! You order lists with sort(), sorted() and reverse().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: sort, sorted with reverse=True and the unchanged original.
tasks.codeTemplate:
zahlen = [5, 2, 8, 1]
kopie = sorted(zahlen, reverse=True)
print(f"Copy: {kopie}")
print(f"Original: {zahlen}")
zahlen.sort()
print(f"Sorted: {zahlen}")

tasks.instruction: The list horses is provided. Sort it with sort() and print it. It must look like this: ['Balu', 'Fox', 'Lightning', 'Luna', 'Stormwind']

The list horses is provided. Create a descending copy copy with sorted(..., reverse=True). Print copy first and then horses – the original stays unchanged: ['Stormwind', 'Luna', 'Lightning', 'Fox', 'Balu'] and ['Stormwind', 'Lightning', 'Luna', 'Fox', 'Balu']
The list horses is provided. Sort it by the length of the entries with sorted(..., key=len) and print the result: ['Fox', 'Luna', 'Balu', 'Stormwind', 'Lightning']

lessonSummary: Great! You loop through lists with for and pass them to functions.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: for loop and enumerate.
The list values = [12, 8, 15, 5] is provided. Add all values with a for loop in the variable total (start 0) and print exactly Total: 40.

lessonSummary: Perfect! You steer loops with break and continue.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: break ends the search, continue skips an entry.
The list horses is provided. Loop through it with for and print every entry as Check: <entry>. If the entry is Luna, then print Found! and end the loop with break.

title: Lesson 9: List comprehension
lessonSummary: Elegant! You build lists in one go.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: transforming and filtering in one line.
tasks.codeTemplate:
schaden = [3, 7, 12, 5]
verdoppelt = [wert * 2 for wert in schaden]
grosse = [wert for wert in schaden if wert > 4]
print(f"Doubled: {verdoppelt}")
print(f"Big: {grosse}")

tasks.instruction: The list numbers = [3, 7, 12, 5] is provided. Build the list doubled (every value times 2) with a list comprehension and print it: [6, 14, 24, 10]
The list numbers = [3, 7, 12, 5] is provided. Build the list big with a list comprehension and an if that only contains values above 4, and print it: [7, 12, 5]
The list horses is provided. Build the list loud with a list comprehension in which every entry is in capital letters via .upper(), and print it: ['STORMWIND', 'LIGHTNING', 'LUNA', 'FOX', 'BALU']
